title: CRLR/225/2012 of MANISH RAWAT Vs SMT. SANGEETA RAWAT

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision (CRLR No. 225 of 2012)
Manish Rawat ...Revisionist
Vs.
Smt. Sangeeta Rawat ...Respondent
Present: None for the parties
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
List revised.
2. None appears to assist the Court. Since being a
Criminal Revision, this Court has got no option except to proceed to
decide the same itself on its own merits.
3. The challenge given by the revisionist-husband in the
present criminal revision is to the impugned order dated 15.09.2012,
as passed by the Principal Judge, Family Court, Pauri Garhwal,
whereby the learned Family Court has partially allowed the
application of the respondent-wife, preferred under Section 125
CrPC, which was registered as Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 106
of 2009, Smt. Sangeeta Rawat v. Manish Rawat, and consequently
had determined the maintenance payable towards the wife @ Rs.
2500/- per month and Rs. 1500/- per month as maintenance towards
the daughter.
4. The grounds taken by the revisionist in the present
criminal revision is that since he is a person of a very meagre
income, he would not be in a position to meet the financial burden of
maintenance of wife and daughter. He further submits that the grant
of maintenance from the date of application itself was not tenable for
the reason being that during the pendency of application under
Section 125 CrPC proceedings, the respondent-wife was already the

2
recipient of the interim maintenance as determined under sub Section
(2) of Section 125 CrPC.
5. The fact of the matter is that as far as the marriage of
13.04.2001 at Kotdwar, the birth of the child (daughter) on
07.05.2003, the fact that the child at that relevant point of time was
studying in Class II, are the facts which are not disputed by the
revisionist in the proceedings before the Court below or even in the
present criminal revision.
6. On the contrary, in order to sustain her application for
maintenance under Section 125 CrPC, the respondent-wife has
contended that the revisionist-husband was having sufficient income
from his engagement which has been disclosed in her application
under Section 125 CrPC, to the effect that the revisionist-husband
was profitably engaged and working in a private firm, and having an
income of about Rs. 7,000/- per month, even as per the statement
recorded by PW1. Irrespective of the fact that even if there being a
meagre income with revisionist-husband , that cannot be a ground of
denying the maintenance to the wife and daughter, he cannot be
legally absolve from the responsibility on that pretext, who are
otherwise legally entitled to receive the maintenance till the marriage
is subsisting and it is not legally dissolved and as a consequence
thereto, the wife gets remarried.
7. For the reasons given by the learned Family Court,
Pauri Garhwal of determining the total maintenance payable @ Rs.
4,000/- to the respondent-wife and her minor daughter as
maintenance is absolutely just and proper as per the present era of
inflation and in proportion to the income, which was proved before
the Court below to be accruing to the revisionist-husband, and hence
the determination made by the learned Family Court for directing the
revisionist to pay the maintenance of total Rs. 4,000/- per month was

3
absolutely just and proper and was in proportion to the income
proved before the Court below, because even otherwise also the wife
and children are entitled to have at least 1/3 of the income of the
husband as maintenance. Even otherwise also, there had been a case
of respondent-wife to the effect that the revisionist-husband is
having his own confectionary shop from where he is having a
handsome income and hence he could easily maintain the wife and
the minor daughter by paying a reasonable amount of maintenance to
them in order to enable them to meet their necessities of life, for a
reasonable living.
8. Consequently, as far as the determination of
maintenance @ Rs. 4,000/- per month is concerned, which has been
made by the Court below, this Court does not find any fault as such
in the grant of maintenance @ Rs. 4,000/- per month, though this
will not prejudice the rights of the respondent-wife to seek an
appropriate enhancement by invoking the provisions contained under
Section 127 CrPC, if at all permissible under law.
9. The issue which has also been pleaded as a ground is
that the same could not be made payable from the date of application
under Section 125 CrPC dated 06.11.2009, on account of the fact
that the respondent-wife was the recipient of an interim maintenance
under Section 125(2) of CrPC, this though as per the view of this
Court cannot be a reason to deny the grant of maintenance from the
date of application, because a determination of maintenance under
sub Section (2) of Section 125 CrPC is only a determination made at
the time when the proceedings before the Court below is pending
consideration as an arrangement during proceedings, but the
payability or the final determination of maintenance would always
be a prerogative of the Family Court to be considered on merits
depending upon the facts and circumstances of the each case as to
whether the amount has to be paid from the date of application or

4
from the date of order which has been statutorily contemplated under
law.
10. The learned Family Court, on considering the
application and assigning the reasoning given therein has rightly
made the direction to pay the amount of maintenance as determined
thus w.e.f. from the date of application i.e. dated 06.11.2009, which
is absolutely appropriate, because the entitlement of a quantum of
maintenance would always be from the date when the claim for
maintenance is actually raised by initiating the proceedings before
the Family Court, which in the instant case happens to be of
06.11.2009. Hence, in that view of the matter, and for the aforesaid
reasons, this Criminal Revision lacks merits and the same is hereby
dismissed accordingly.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 02.01.2020
Mahinder/
